title: Latency quantile probe lab notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lab-style playbook for designing small synthetic probes that exercise latency quantiles across multi-tenant inference serving paths. Goal is to: 1) get repeatable signal for p50/p90/p99 under controlled cache/cold-start scenarios; 2) test tenant-priority weighting for dashboard alerting and cost allocation; 3) validate sampling budget impact on trace usefulness.

Experiment setup summary:
- Environment: staging inference cluster (dedicated test pool, same kernel selection as prod).
- Workloads: fanout=1 (single-model) and fanout=3 (multi-model routing) runs. Sequence length buckets: short(<=64), medium(65-512), long(>512).
- Cache states: cold (empty KV), warm-prefix (fixed prefix warmed), warmed-KV (kv cache filled with realistic session traces).
- Load profile: steady QPS 20, 100, 400 for low/med/high. Burst injections to simulate traffic spikes.

Metrics to collect (explicit definitions):
- request.latency.ms.quantile_p50: end-to-end time from request received to last token emitted (ms).
- request.latency.ms.quantile_p90: same as above for p90.
- request.latency.ms.quantile_p99: 99th percentile measured over minute windows.
- kv.cache.hit_rate: fraction of requests served from prefix/KV reads. (note: tag by model and tenant)
- model.fanout.count: number of models resolved for a request (1..N).
- route.fallback.count: number of requests that fell back to cheaper/compatible model.
- trace.sampled: boolean flag if trace recorded (post-sampling).
- tenant.weighted_latency_ms: weighted latency that multiplies request.latency by tenant-priority factor (see below).

Trace anchoring & sampling plan:
- Anchor traces at model-load, kv-eviction, and fallback decision points. Use lightweight span names: model.resolve, kv.lookup, compile/kernels, emitter.write.
- Adaptive sampling rule: keep 100% traces for p99 tail candidates (detect via real-time p99 probe), baseline sample 1% for p50, 5% for p90. Coordinator service will mark candidate requests using a small in-probe estimator.

Tenant-priority weighting heuristic (for dashboards/alerts):
- Assign each tenant a priority score (0.1 low — 2.0 high) maintained in config service.
- tenant.weighted_latency_ms = request.latency.ms * priority_score. This biases alerting toward high-value tenants while retaining raw SLI visibility.
- For alert thresholds, monitor both raw p99 and weighted p95. Alert if weighted p95 exceeds SLO threshold for two consecutive minutes.

Dashboard panel suggestions (compact):
- Latency quantile matrix: rows=tenants (top 10 by QPS), cols=sequence length buckets, panels show p50/p90/p99.
- Probe provenance heatmap: axis=cache state vs QPS, cell=observed p99; overlay trace-sampled count.
- Tenant-weighted alert preview: show ratio of weighted to raw p95 for top tenants.
- Fanout impact stream: stacked area of model.fanout.count vs latency quantiles.

Acceptance criteria for rollout of probe into prod sampling: 
- Synthetic probe can reproduce p99 within +/- 8% of controlled-run median across three repeats.
- Traces collected by adaptive sampler include at least 80% of root causes seen in full-trace baseline (measured via offline replay).
- Tenant-weighted alerting reduces noisy ops alerts by >= 40% in test window while preserving alerts for high-priority tenants.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost: high trace volume if adaptive estimator misclassifies tails. Add quota clamp per minute.
- Cardinality: top-tenants matrix OK, but rollout for mid-long tail tenants may need aggregation to tiered-buckets.
- Cold-start safety: ensure probes don’t distort allocator scaling decisions — mark probes with debug header so autoscaler excludes them.

Next steps & action items:
- [Marcus Li] implement probe harness and estimator shim (due 2025-07-25).
- [Aisha Patel] dashboard wireframes + sample queries (due 2025-07-30).
- [Evelyn Park] run 3 repeated experiments and capture baseline traces (due 2025-08-01).

Notes to self: keep probe scale small initially; use tenant header test-tenant:X to avoid billing/chargeback noise. Save raw exporter output to ephemeral object store for replay analysis.

References:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-4232: telemetry standard for inference stacks
- JIRA-OBS-1127: sampling budget feature ticket
